content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "F-35 C2D2 (program element 0604840F) is a U.S. Air Force research-and-development program funded in the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b099d1eda670839d"}}, {"text": "The program funds the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter's Continuous Capability Development and Delivery (C2D2) effort, which delivers incremental warfighting-capability improvements to keep the aircraft ahead of evolving threats across three variants: the F-35A conventional takeoff and landing, the F-35B short takeoff and vertical landing, and the F-35C carrier variant.", "citation": {"fact_id": "68690938ba32ad9c"}}, {"text": "The current focus of the work is fielding the F-35's Block 4 modernization, a package of new software capabilities, upgraded aircraft hardware, and new weapons integration; the Block 4 Capability Development Document was approved by the Joint Requirements Oversight Council on 21 March 2017.", "citation": {"fact_id": "68690938ba32ad9c"}}, {"text": "A major hardware line within the program is Technology Refresh 3 (TR-3), which develops and certifies new F-35 core subsystems — the Integrated Core Processor, Aircraft Memory System, and Panoramic Cockpit Display units — needed to host all Block 4 capabilities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e9e78eec9d5c5ac9"}}, {"text": "The program also funds the Power Thermal Management Upgrade (PTMU), which adds cooling and power capacity — larger heat exchangers, higher pump speeds, and reconfigured liquid loops — because Block 4 and later capabilities exceed the aircraft's original thermal-management design.", "citation": {"fact_id": "09b5632049bcd97c"}}, {"text": "Other work covers the F-35's logistics software, transitioning from the legacy Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS) to the modern Operational Data Integrated Network (ODIN) to manage maintenance, supply chain, and mission data across the fleet.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e6260e56fab05319"}}, {"text": "Propulsion development in the program modernizes the F135 engine through the Engine Core Upgrade, intended to recapture engine life and add power and cooling headroom for future mission-system enhancements across the global F-35 fleet.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b9d2e1c264889ec3"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding is $1,182,094 thousand (about $1.18 billion) requested for FY2026, up from $1,134,207 thousand enacted in FY2025.", "citation": {"fact_id": "aa918dacafc68ca7"}}, {"text": "That is a year-over-year increase of $47,887 thousand (roughly $48 million) from FY2025 to FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "db62f69ce9d54f56"}}, {"text": "In FY2024 the program recorded actual spending of $1,236,710 thousand (about $1.24 billion), so the FY2026 request is slightly below the program's recent execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "87d757ad2dea1408"}}, {"text": "The entire FY2026 request is discretionary funding — the R-1 exhibit shows a discretionary request of $1,182,094 thousand and no separate reconciliation (mandatory) request for this program element.", "citation": {"fact_id": "379f24a7da048064"}}, {"text": "The program is entirely modernization-focused: it sits in the Air Force's development portfolio for upgrading an already-fielded aircraft, funding the Block 4 releases that add weapons, sensors, and software capability to keep the F-35 relevant against emerging threats.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a3fe4415d6d99694"}}, {"text": "Test and evaluation is a large cost driver, funding integrated flight testing at government sites including Nellis AFB, Edwards AFB, and MCAS Yuma to validate incremental software releases and weapon integrations before they reach the fleet.", "citation": {"fact_id": "788ff8de03f48a84"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force appropriation, and it is a joint F-35 effort serving the Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps, and international partner countries.", "citation": {"fact_id": "68690938ba32ad9c"}}, {"text": "The F-35 Joint Program Office manages the effort, with acquisition and product-support workforce costs (including AFLCMC civilian pay) funded within the program element to oversee development across the air vehicle, propulsion, combat data, maintenance, and training systems.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ba56bb9ea2438150"}}, {"text": "Prime contractor Lockheed Martin Aeronautics and its subcontractors perform flight-test and technology-refresh work under the Development Foundation Contract at Edwards Air Force Base, Pax River Naval Air Station, and the Fort Worth, Texas laboratory.", "citation": {"fact_id": "17cf4d3a642b0418"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
